There are no flies in the ointment of the overwhelming touring success of Noah Kahan . The fan enthusiasm that led to across-the-board sellouts for his “Great Divide World Tour” this past summer is highly likely to continue when his “The Last of the Bugs World Tour” hits stadiums in North America and Europe in the spring and summer of 2027. The highly anticipated dates were announced Thursday morning as an online countdown clock drew to a close.
The North American leg of the Live Nation-promoted tour will begin April 24 in Athens, Georgia’s Sanford Stadium, and continue through June 18 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. Along the way, Kahan will do four nights in a row at Boston’s historic Fenway Park, slated for May 29 through June 2, a repeat of the record-breaking four-night stand he did at his hometown ballpark this past year. Other shows across the continent are set for Detroit, Las Vegas, San Francisco, Montreal, Nashville, Tampa, Birmingham, Charlotte, Houston, Austin, Columbus, Madison and Norman, Oklahoma.
After wrapping up in North America in mid-June, Kahan will head to Europe starting July 1, with shows in Germany, Italy, the U.K. and other countries. Shows include stops at Berlin’s Waldbühne, Seville’s Plaza de España and Paris’ Hippodrome ParisLongchamp. The last six dates on the tour, with stops at London’s Wembley Stadium and in Dublin and Glasgow, were the only ones previously announced prior to Thursday. (Scroll down for the full list of shows.)
The presales for North American shows begins Nov. 10 at noon local time. To participate, fans must sign up here by Nov. 5 at 11:59 p.m. ET. A general onsale for all dates around the world then takes place on Nov. 12 at noon local time, at NoahKahan.com/pages/tour .

“Artist presales for this tour are hosted by multiple ticketing sites, but anyone who signs up can join the sale,” the announcement stated. For the artist presale on Ticketmaster, no code is needed, as access is tied to the holder’s account, whereas presales hosted on other sites may require a code for access.
The announcement further said, “Working in partnership with Ticketmaster, extra protections will be in place to help block bad actors from signing up for the Artist Presale. Some fans may be asked to complete a quick selfie check, or in rare cases, provide an ID via Persona to sign up.”
A special presale for the MetLife Stadium show in New Jersey will be held for fans who held tickets to the Citi Feld show that was canceled this past July 18. Those ticketholders will have access to a two-hour presale taking place Nov. 10 from 9-11 a.m. ET.
A “Reserved by Spotify” presale for North American shows will begin Nov. 11 at 9 a.m. local time. Those tickets will be available to eligible U.S. Spotify Premium subscribers through Ticketmaster; fans will be notified by Spotify via email and app notification about how to purchase up to two tickets through that program.
In North America, Kahan will be using the Face Value Exchange program, which mandates that tickets purchased on Ticketmaster are nontransferable and can only be resold for face value on that ticketing site. (The exception is the Buffalo show, since New York law prohibits making tickets nontransferable.)
For the European shows, an artist presale will take place Laylo, beginning Nov. 10 at noon local time. Fans can sign up here by Nov. 9th at 5 p.m. local time to access the presale. As with the American shows, the general onsale for remaining tickets will then be on Nov. 12.
There haven’t been many breaks in Kahan’s touring activity. At the end of August, he wrapped up the North American leg of the “Great Divide” tour. It included his biggest show to date at the Rose Bowl, where he performed to 65,000 fans in August. This came on the heels of Kahan becoming the first artist ever to headline and sell out four straight nights at Fenway.
He has plenty of concert activity still on the agenda before the end of this year, in addition to the ’27 dates just announced. Following a tour of Australia and New Zealand in September and October he just wrapped up, November and the first half of December of this year will find Kahan playing arenas in the U.K., Germany, Denmark, France, Ireland, Switzerland and Scotland.
Kahan is expected to be in Grammy contention in the coming months for his fourth studio album, “The Great Divide,” which gave his 2026 tour its name. The next tour is named after the deluxe version of the album, which was subtitled “The Last of the Bugs.” He is the only artist to have had two albums in the top 10 of the Billboard 200 for each of the past six weeks, those albums being “The Great Divide” and its breakthrough predecessor, the five-times-platinum “Stick Season.”
Kahan’s sold-out stadium show in Pasadena this past August was enthusiastically reviewed by Variety in a review titled “Noah Kahan Turns His ‘Miserable’ Material Into Manic Elation at Triumphant Rose Bowl Stadium Show: Concert Review.”
